versions.short: The bill would direct the FAA head to update aviation regulations within 18 months so that pilots, air traffic controllers and other aviation workers are encouraged to seek help for mental health conditions and to disclose them. It would require the FAA to regularly review its special issuance process for mental health medications and treatments for pilots and air traffic controllers, and to expand training for aviation medical examiners. It would authorize up to $15,000,000 per fiscal year from 2026 through 2028 for the Office of Aerospace Medicine to hire and train more examiners, including psychiatrists, and to clear a backlog of cases. It would require the FAA to implement, where appropriate, recommendations from a 2024 aviation rulemaking committee on mental health and medical clearances, with justification to Congress for any it declines to adopt. Finally, it would require a public information campaign from 2026 through 2028 to reduce stigma around seeking mental health care in aviation and to make support services more widely known.
